To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
otolith edge chemistry can be used to identify the region of capture of fully marine fish in oceanic waters.

the otolith elemental signatures of Patagonian Toothfish (Dissotichus eleginoids) captured in two different regions (Antarctic and South America) were distinct and that the signatures of fish captured within each region also differed, indicating that the otoliths record the capture location of this oceanic fish.

1) otolith elemental signatures discriminate fish from different geographic regions with near complete success; 2) signatures discriminate fish from within geographic regions with moderate success; 3) signatures are consistent between fish of the same age class and sex; 4) signatures vary by season, but not by depth; and 5) otolith elemental composition is not affected by the capture method (longline versus bottom trawl) or the time of year when the fish were sampled.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of otolith elemental signatures as a tool for reconstructing the environmental history experienced during the life of fish and for discriminating the geographic provenance and migration patterns of fish.

the use of elemental signatures in fish otoliths for the reconstruction of the life history of Patagonian Toothfish (Dissotichus eleginodes) and the use of otolith chemistry for stock identification of Patagonian and Antarctic Toothfish.
the application of otolith chemistry to the study of the life history of a fully marine fish.

otolith elemental composition can be used as a tool for reconstructing the environmental history of fully marine fish, such as Patagonian toothfsh, and can be applied to other species in the future.
otoliths are capable of recording spatial information for both estuarine and oceanic fish.

otolith chemistry can be used to discriminate the geographic provenances of fully oceanic species.
otoliths of oceanic fish can record the capture site and thus can be used to reconstruct the movement history of fully marine fish in open-ocean environments.
otolith elemental composition is a useful tool for reconstructing the capture site of toothfish, which is important for fisheries management and conservation of the species and its habitat.
